newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P 500s post record high, end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P 500s post record high, end higher.

text.p: U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures surged into record territory and above key 800.00 to reach as high as 807.50 in a huge broad market rebound.
Techs, transports, financials, gold miners and energy shares rallied sharply, in contrast to a lethargic tone in U.S. debt futures amid this week's quarterly refunding.

S&P traders noted that March was resilient early, even amid IBM weakness after three firms cut profit estimates for the company. Traders said bullish followthrough from Tuesday's late S&P rally underpinned the market early and eventually pushed it through key 800.00.
One S&P trader had predicted, "If we trade 797.00 we're going to fly."

Indeed, several traders noted that the decisive move above resistance in the 796.00 handle and buystops above 797.00 helped propel March S&P through the old record at 799.70 and into psychologically key 800.00.

"After the auction results came off we came down to 797.00-even and then turned back up," the trader said. "So it was a key level both ways," he said, adding that the bent of this market has been to make former resistance levels quickly into support.

"More importantly we didn't really break down with the OTC when it went down the last couple of days," another trader said. He said March S&Ps' ability to hold amid recent tech sector losses was a sign of resilience. When technology stocks rebounded late Tuesday and again today, already stable S&Ps soared, he said.
Volume in March S&Ps just after the close was estimated on Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards at 86,000 contracts, traders reported.
They said fast-market status was implemented several times during the afternoon's rally.
Bulls put upside targets now at 811.50, 813.00, 815.00 and 816.00.

At the end of pit trading, March S&Ps were up 12.40 points to 807.25, Value Lines were 7.75 higher at 714.20, NYSE Composites were 5.75 higher at 422.45, Nikkeis were 435 higher at 18,645, Midcap 400s were up 4.10 at 267.80 and Nasdaq 100s were up 25.00 at 906.75.
